about: Engine lineage for the dashboard's Engine Performance tab (display only; read by engine/engine_performance.py). Update at every release. Figures are copied from benchmarks/engine_v2/RELEASES.md, the release manifests and gates, and the research ledgers named in 'source'. Log-likelihood gains are per race on identical races; fit = how much better than random the winner's chance was.

identical_races.label: Same 4,730 Queensland races, 2025-26 (each version fitted only on races before 2025)
identical_races.caveat: 2025-26 was examined many times while these versions were built, so these figures overstate what each step will deliver live. Part of the v2.0 to v2.1.1 gain is the larger database (Queensland country results), not the engine alone.

families.comparison_basis: Production and previous engine are scored from the same morning fields snapshot and the same history cutoff; the previous engine is scored a few minutes after the production set is published, before the first race. Paired on races both saved before the start and settled. Ledger chances are raw model chances renormalised over the runners that ran.

checkpoints_proposed.status: Proposed 27 Nov 2026 (no checkpoints were found agreed in the register); for Damo to confirm
checkpoints_proposed.rule: Review each paired comparison at 300, 1,000 and 2,000 settled paired races per state group. At each review report the gain per race with its 95% interval, top pick and winner-in-top-3 differences, and consistency by state and by fortnight. A checkpoint is a review, never an automatic promotion.
checkpoints_proposed.why: The per-race spread of the difference between two engines is about 0.15, so the 95% interval is roughly +/-0.017 at 300 races, +/-0.009 at 1,000 and +/-0.007 at 2,000. Gains of the size measured in research (0.005 to 0.017 per race) need 1,000 to 2,000 races to tell apart from noise; the expected live gain is usually smaller than the research figure.
